title: Adaptive log chunking & trace stitcher for low-latency multi-tenant ingestion
creator: Maya Jensen
description:
Problem: Large structured log payloads (stack traces, user-submitted JSON blobs, serialized spans) create amplification and high tail latency in our ingestion pipeline. Fragmented events across network and gateway boundaries lose trace continuity, making it hard to correlate logs with traces and leading to noisy dashboards.

Goal: Implement a resilient ingestion component that: (1) splits oversized log events into ordered, size-bounded chunks at the edge; (2) attaches minimal sequencing metadata and checksums; (3) reassembles chunks (stitcher) in the core ingest service with timeout-driven fallback for partial payloads; (4) preserves a single canonical trace_id/span_id mapping for stitched payloads and surfaces stitching metrics to the Console. The feature must be tenant-aware (per-tenant chunking policies), support both Loki-style streams and ELK-style documents, and play nicely with existing backpressure and autoscaling controls.
acceptance_criteria: Edge gateways split payloads > 256KB into ordered chunks and add X-Chunk-Id, X-Chunk-Seq, X-Chunk-Checksum headers
Core ingest stitcher reassembles chunks within 30s default window; emits stitched document with original payload and a stitching.status field (complete | partial | timed_out)
Stitched documents retain single trace_id and map to a canonical log_id and event_sequence metadata for downstream correlation
If chunk reassembly fails after the window, we persist partial payload + metadata and produce a placeholder record that links partial pieces in Console UI
No increase in median ingest latency for single-chunk documents (<= 5ms added P50), and 95th percentile tail for large multi-chunk events reduced vs current baseline
Integration tests for Loki and ELK sinks verify ordering and trace continuity across shard/partition boundaries
Operational dashboards added: chunking.rate, stitcher.success_rate, stitcher.timeout_rate, partial-events-per-tenant, chunking-induced-retries
Feature gated behind runtime flag per-environment and per-tenant config; rollout plan validated on staging before prod enablement
risks: Ordering guarantees across tenant-sharded Kafka topics may require adding sequence watermarking; potential re-sharding impact
Large number of small chunks could increase metadata overhead and throughput costs if misconfigured
Partial reassembly persistence increases storage and retention considerations for regulated tenants
Interactions with existing KV cache and batching logic could cause unexpected latencies during high-concurrency reassembly
rollout_plan: 1) Implement feature behind feature-flag and tenant-config in staging
2) Run synthetic load tests with mixed payload sizes and compare P50/P95/P99 tail latency to baseline
3) Enable for 3 low-traffic tenants with sampling=100% for 48h, observe stitcher metrics and storage impact
4) Ramp to 30% of tenants for 7 days with sampling and per-tenant size thresholds, monitor error budgets
5) Full enablement with adjustable defaults and automated cleanup for timed_out partials
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: partial-events-per-tenant growth > 50% day-over-day -> notify observability team
Dashboard: per-tenant chunking.rate, stitcher.success_rate, average-reassembly-latency, storage-overhead-by-tenant
implementation_notes: Chunking scheme: target max_chunk_payload=256KB, sequence numbers as 64-bit monotonic per-original-event, CRC32 checksum per chunk
Edge behavior: prefer coalescing when multiple small events arrive within 10ms to reduce per-request overhead
Stitcher idempotency: use canonical event_id + chunk_seq to dedupe retries; support at-least-once chunk delivery semantics
Persistence: store in RocksDB-backed reassembly buffer with TTL configured per-tenant (default 60s), write partials to cold S3 when TTL expires
Compatibility: when incoming document already contains trace_id/span_id, stitcher must preserve; otherwise generate synthetic trace_id and emit mapping to trace service
